findings.problem: The pictogram (main road with a branch joining from the lower right) is the Vienna/RTA 'traffic merges from the right ahead' sign: you are on the main road and OTHER vehicles join it. Name and meaning say the opposite (your road merges and you must merge), and it breaks symmetry with w-merge-left, which is correctly 'vehicles merge from the left'. Note: with the fixed meaning it overlaps i-lane-joining; the two list each other in `confuse`, so an auto question can show two correct names. Drop them from each other's confuse lists.
findings.evidence: EDI guidance chart (RTA-licensed) lists this group as 'Traffic merges from the left ahead' (web search snippet of edi-uae.com 20191126 chart); Vienna Convention merging-traffic warning sign; the file's own draw text

findings.problem: The draw text (and the drawn symbol) shows horizontal beam lines, which is the ISO main-beam (high beam) symbol. Tunnels and low-visibility sections need DIPPED headlights; high beam in a tunnel dazzles others. The action does not say which lights, so the picture teaches high beam. Redraw with beam lines slanting DOWN (ISO 7000-0083 dipped beam) and say dipped beam in the action. The project's own fig-beam-low/fig-beam-high use the same low/high distinction.
findings.evidence: ISO 7000-0082 (main beam, horizontal lines) vs 0083 (dipped beam, lines slanting down); dipped headlights are the rule in tunnels (general driving guidance, e.g. UK/EU tunnel rules; no UAE text says high beam). Draw field cannot be patched here: drawing agent must change src/signs/mandatory.js m-headlights-on

findings.problem: The name 'يجب أن تسير بهذا الاتجاه' is true of every blue mandatory direction sign. The auto question generator fills distractors from the same category (mandatory) and from confuse (m-turn-right, m-keep-right), so for m-turn-right / m-ahead-only / m-turn-left pictures this option can appear and is also correct; and for this sign's picture (blue rectangle, arrow right) the option 'السير باتجاه اليمين فقط' is also correct. On the shape question: keep the rectangle. The RTA/institute charts put 'You must go this way' in the CONTROL signs group together with Stop, Give Way, Give way to pedestrians and No Entry, separate from the blue-circle mandatory group, which fits a blue rectangular arrow board rather than a blue disc (a disc with a right arrow is already m-turn-right). Consider cat 'priority'/control and a name that includes the board shape.
findings.evidence: GMDC Guidance Chart (gmdc.ae, search snippet): 'CONTROL SIGNS Stop, You must give way to pedestrians, Give Way, No Entry, You must go this way'; RTA Arabic 2012 captions list يجب أن تسير بهذا الاتجاه separately from يجب أن تسير باتجاه اليمين فقط (research/signs.md finding 2)

findings.problem: The name 'ممنوع تجاوز الشاحنات' reads naturally as 'you may not overtake trucks' (trucks as object). The sign (red lorry on the left) means trucks are not allowed to overtake, which is what `meaning` says. A beginner will pick the wrong reading.
findings.evidence: Vienna Convention C,13ba (no overtaking by goods vehicles); the item's own meaning

findings.problem: The action and uae_note teach 1.5 m as an RTA requirement, but the app's own lesson cards (q_rules rules-card-031 and rules-card-067, fig-bike-gap) teach 'at least 1 m' citing the RTA LMV handbooks. A learner gets two different numbers. I could not open the RTA 'Driving Safely in Dubai' booklet (S2) to confirm the 1.5 m; the 1.5 m figure found online is a safe-cycling campaign (Cycle Safe Dubai), not a rule with a fine. Align both files on one sourced figure; until then, state the handbook minimum and treat 1.5 m as advice.
findings.evidence: Gulf News 'Live and let live is message of safe-cycling advocates in UAE' (1.5 m is an advocacy call); q_rules.json rules-card-031/067 (1 m, src RTA LMV handbook 7th ed and 3rd ed Arabic)

findings.problem: The draw puts the days 'السبت - الخميس' on the plate, the pre-2022 pattern with Friday free. Since the 2022 weekend change, Dubai paid parking is charged Monday to Saturday and is free on Sunday, so the picture shows an outdated example. Change the second line of the drawing to الاثنين - السبت, or drop the days line.
findings.evidence: RTA announcement Dec 2021/Jan 2022: paid parking free on Sundays, charged Monday to Saturday (widely reported, e.g. Khaleej Times, Gulf News 2022)

findings.problem: Not settled from a Dubai source: all sources agree on a falcon emblem on blue signs, but the colours (blue fill, gold numerals) come only from the Abu Dhabi TR-538 standard. The uae_note is fine. Keep confidence at medium, or keep high only for the fact that E routes use a falcon emblem, not for the colours.
findings.evidence: Gulf News 2006 and AARoads/Wikipedia snippets: 'number within a falcon emblem'; no Dubai colour spec reachable

findings.problem: The D-route shield design is only partly confirmed: sources agree on a fort emblem with D and 2 or 3 digits on green Dubai signs; the colours in the draw (green fill, white numerals) were not confirmed by any source. The example is correct: D 94 is Jumeirah Beach Road (renamed King Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud Street).
findings.evidence: Wikipedia D 94 road / Dubai route numbering system (search snippets): 'emblem of a fort, the letter D and a two or three digit number'

findings.problem: The draw uses an adult holding a child's hand, which is the UK 'pedestrian zone' pictogram. The Vienna and RTA mandatory 'pedestrians only' disc shows a single walking pedestrian. This is a drawing detail only.
findings.evidence: Vienna Convention mandatory 'compulsory footpath' sign (single pedestrian); RTA charts follow the Vienna form

findings.problem: Open question on direction. The drawing (src/signs/markings.js, comment 'chevrons pointing in the direction of travel') puts the V apex DOWNSTREAM, away from approaching drivers. The US MUTCD, on which the cited Abu Dhabi TR-511 is based, requires the point of each gore chevron to face TOWARD approaching traffic. I could not read TR-511 section 657 itself or a Dubai source, so this is not proven for the UAE. The meaning and action text are fine.
findings.evidence: MUTCD 3B.24: 'Chevron markings shall be white, with the point of each chevron facing toward approaching traffic' (gore areas); research/markings.md S23 names 'chevron marking 657'

findings.problem: Meaning says the broken centre line may be crossed 'for overtaking only'. A broken centre line may also be crossed to turn left into a side road or entrance when safe. With 'فقط' the learner will reject a correct exam option about turning across it.
findings.evidence: RTA LMV handbook (S1) line rules: broken lines may be crossed when safe; Executive Regulations Art. 58 (S2) restricts only continuous lines
